subject: Gender & Sexuality Studies
selected_point: Sexual dimorphism in African elephants: male long thick tusks vs female short thin tusks
posted_prompt: Show two African elephants side-by-side; the one on the left is female, and the one on the right is male. Please observe and compare the morphological differences between the two elephants; the image primarily shows the elephants from the front.

manual: Instructions for the Observation Experiment: Sexual Dimorphism in African ElephantsI. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Sexual Dimorphism in African Elephants: Comparison of Male and Female Tusks2. Subject: Humanities and Social Sciences – Gender & Sexuality Studies3. Experiment Objective: To observe and understand sexual dimorphism in African elephants by comparing morphological differences, especially tusk length and thickness, between a female and a male elephant using visual evidence.II. Experimental MaterialsHigh-resolution image or video showing two African elephants side-by-side from the front; observation record sheet (optional).III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Ensure the image/video clearly shows two African elephants positioned side-by-side, viewed primarily from the front.2. Identification: Confirm that the elephant on the left is female and the elephant on the right is male.3. Core Observation: Carefully observe the tusks of both elephants, focusing on length, thickness, and overall prominence. Note additional frontal morphological cues such as head width and body robustness if visible.4. Comparison: Compare the observed traits between the left (female) and right (male) elephants, recording similarities and differences.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. The female elephant on the left displays relatively short and thin tusks.2. The male elephant on the right displays noticeably longer and thicker tusks that extend further forward.3. When viewed from the front, the contrast in tusk size is clear and consistent between the two elephants.V. Summary of Experimental PrinciplesAfrican elephants exhibit sexual dimorphism, meaning males and females differ in physical traits. One of the most prominent differences is tusk morphology: males typically develop longer and thicker tusks due to genetic, hormonal, and social selection factors, while females usually have shorter and thinner tusks. This visual comparison demonstrates how biological sex influences physical form in non-human animals.VI. NotesThis is an observational experiment with no physical manipulation. Accurate identification and clear frontal perspective are essential for correct conclusions.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Sexual dimorphism in African elephants, defined by consistent biological differences between males and females, especially tusk length and thickness. Minimum assumptions: elephants are African elephants; left is female, right is male; frontal view allows tusk comparison. Expected phenomena storyline: (1) establish stable side-by-side frontal view; (2) identify left as female and right as male; (3) visually compare tusks; (4) observe female’s shorter thinner tusks versus male’s longer thicker tusks; (5) infer sexual dimorphism as the causal explanation. Visibility constraints: tusks must be fully visible from the front with stable left-right orientation for verification.
